title: Tools: github.workflow.dispatch and github.runs.status, tested against a fake GitHub API
goal: Two governed tools that start an allow-listed workflow and read its recent runs through the GitHub REST API
acceptance: github.workflow.dispatch posts workflow_dispatch only for an allow-listed repository + workflow + ref; anything else is refused before any network call; it is registered as write-external and needs a grant
github.runs.status returns the latest runs of an allow-listed workflow (status, conclusion, created and updated times, URL) and is read-only and Green

Tests against a fake GitHub API on loopback: dispatch sends the right request and Authorization header; a refused pair makes no call; 401, 403, 404, 422, a rate limit and a timeout give bounded errors that never echo the token; status parses runs
The token is read from the private file at call time and never logged, returned or put in an error
privacy: Neutral invented repositories, workflows and runs in tests; the GitHub token never in git, config.json, tests, logs, chat or the relocation snapshot.
escalation: A wider token scope or another repository on the allow-list goes to the owner

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-26: two small REST tools on the existing executor and grant registry, with a loopback fake server. Not a measurement.
